tools.name: call
tools.title: Call the human
tools.description:
Ring the human's phone (iPhone or Android), read `question` aloud word
    for word, and return what they say back as text. Waits up to ~30s.

    status "completed" carries their words in `transcript` (empty if they only
    listened). "ringing" (not picked up yet) or "in_call" (listening) means the
    call has not settled: pass call_id to poll_result until it does. An
    unanswered ring settles as "missed" within about a minute; "declined" means
    they refused it. Do not retry an unanswered call in a loop: send one `text`
    instead.

    By default the line stays open after their answer ("open": true): they hear
    a soft hold sound while you think, and a voice assistant tells them you are
    working on it. Reply with `say`, finish with `hang_up`; after about two
    minutes of silence the line drops by itself. Anything they said while
    waiting comes back with their next answer as "said_while_waiting". The
    "language" and "language_name" fields report what the recognizer heard, as
    information only. `voice` picks who speaks (female first: bella, sarah,
    jessica, ...; male: roger, eric, brian, ...) and sticks for later calls.

    Reuse the returned session_token in later calls and texts so the phone
    keeps one thread. The `from` in the result is your own number: never call
    or text it. Missing `to` returns setup_required with download links.

question.description: What to say, read aloud word for word, up to 2000 characters (about two minutes). It need not be a question: a status update or a summary works too.
question.title: Question

to.description: The human's 10-digit Call Me number, from My Number in the app (not a regular phone number). Local clients read it from ~/.aiphone/config.json user_number. In a host without file access, reuse a number given earlier in this chat, but do not claim it is saved across chats. Omit it only to get setup_required with the download links.
to.title: To

from_label.description: Who is calling, shown on their phone and spoken: e.g. "Claude on my laptop".
from_label.title: From Label

session_token.description: A session_token from an earlier result, to stay in that thread. Omit on first contact.
session_token.title: Session Token

keep_open.description: The line always stays up after their answer so you can reply with `say`; end it with `hang_up`. Kept for older clients: false no longer makes a one-shot call.
keep_open.title: Keep Open

language.description: The language you are speaking, e.g. "tr", "pt-BR" or "Turkish". The call's own short lines (thanks, goodbye) follow it. Empty means English, or on `say` keeps the current one.
language.title: Language

voice.description: Who speaks, female first (default "bella"). female: bella, sarah, jessica, matilda, laura, alice (british), lily (british); neutral: river; male: roger, eric, chris, brian, will, liam, bill, george (british), daniel (british), charlie (australian). "female" or "male" picks the first of that kind. Your choice sticks for this session's later calls until you pass another; empty keeps it, or else uses the voice the person chose in their app.
voice.title: Voice

tools.name: hang_up
tools.title: Hang up
tools.description:
End a call you placed. In an open conversation `goodbye` is spoken
    first; leave it empty to just hang up. A call that already ended reports
    its final status.

call_id.description: The call_id from the call or play_audio result.
call_id.title: Call Id

session_token.description: The session_token from an earlier result. It keeps every call and text in one thread on their phone.
session_token.title: Session Token

goodbye.description: Spoken before the line drops in an open conversation, e.g. "Thanks, I'll get on it." Empty just hangs up.
goodbye.title: Goodbye

tools.name: play_audio
tools.title: Play long audio
tools.description:
Bigger and longer audio goes here. Calls the human and plays a
    recording to them as a phone call: a podcast, a long narration you
    rendered, a voice memo, music. `source` is a link (YouTube, SoundCloud, a
    podcast page, or a direct .mp3/.m4a/.wav/.ogg/.flac/... link) or the
    audio_id of a file uploaded with
    `curl --data-binary @file.m4a "https://callmemcp.com/audio?to=<number>&filename=file.m4a"`
    (up to 300 MB / 3 hours, kept for a day). The voice says your `intro`, the
    title and the length, then asks if they want to listen now; on a yes the
    file plays as plain sound (no voice model) until it ends or they hang up.
    Returns once they answer the offer: status "playing" (they said yes),
    "completed" with listened:false (no, or nothing), or missed/declined.
    poll_result later reports listened_s and finished. Use `call` for text
    under ~2000 characters. `language` ("tr", "de") is the language of your
    intro; the offer and the call's own lines follow it.

source.description: A link (YouTube, SoundCloud, a podcast page, or a direct .mp3/.m4a/.wav/.ogg/.flac link) or the audio_id of an uploaded file.
source.title: Source

tools.name: poll_result
tools.title: Get call result
tools.description:
Check on a call that came back "ringing", "in_call" or "playing". Waits
    up to ~25s for it to settle, then returns the same shape as `call`: the
    final status and transcript once they answer, decline, or the ring times
    out ("missed", within about a minute). Still not settled: call it again.
    For play_audio calls it reports listened_s and finished. Rings nothing.

session_token.title: Session Token

tools.name: say
tools.title: Say the next line
tools.description:
In a call whose result came back "open": true, speak `text` to the human
    and return what they answer, in the same shape as `call`. Only after their
    previous answer is in. Waits up to ~30s; on "in_call", follow up with
    poll_result. "open": false means the call has ended. Pass `language` only
    to switch the language of the call's own lines; empty keeps it. `voice`
    switches who speaks from this line on (female first: bella, sarah, ...;
    male: roger, eric, ...); empty keeps it. Anything
    they said while you were thinking comes back as "said_while_waiting".
    End the call with `hang_up` once you are done.

Name this session's conversation thread on the human's phone (e.g. the

tools.name: setup
tools.title: Set up Call Me
tools.description:
Return first-setup instructions and clickable App Store and Google Play
    download links, for when you do not have the human's Call Me number yet.
    Show both links to the human as clickable links, then ask them to open My
    Number in the app and give you its 10 digits. Nothing is sent and nothing
    rings.

tools.name: text
tools.title: Text the human
tools.description:
Send a one-way text to the human's phone (a push notification, no
    ring). Use it for updates that need no answer, or as the fallback when a
    call comes back "missed" or "declined". delivered:false means it was saved
    to their history but no notification showed; `notice` says why. Their
    replies arrive through wait_for_reply. Missing `to` returns setup_required
    with the download links. Pass a previous session_token to stay in the
    same thread.

body.description: The message, up to 2000 characters. Markdown links render as links.
body.title: Body

tools.name: wait_for_reply
tools.title: Wait for a text reply
tools.description:
Wait for the human to send something back to this session — texts and
    voicemail transcripts arrive here. Long-polls up to wait_s (max 30s);
    returns {events, cursor}. Pass the returned cursor next time to only see
    new events. An empty events list just means nothing yet — poll again if
    you are still waiting.

session_token.description: The session_token from an earlier result. It keeps every call and text in one thread on their phone.
session_token.title: Session Token

cursor.description: The cursor from the previous result; 0 the first time.
cursor.title: Cursor

wait_s.description: How long to wait for something to arrive, 0 to 30 seconds.
wait_s.title: Wait S
